前端必须实现：
- 请求参数仅使用 page 和 page_size（两者为整数）。前端不得发送 skip 或 limit；如果用户/代码尝试发送 skip 或 limit，应阻止发送并在本地报错/记录，或者在收到 422 时给出清晰提示（后端会拒绝）。
- 验证与缺省值：
  - page：整数，最小 1，缺省 1。  [FACT:request-page-type] [FACT:request-page-minimum] [FACT:request-page-default]
  - page_size：整数，范围 1—50，缺省 20。  [FACT:request-page-size-type] [FACT:request-page-size-minimum] [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default]
- 不要在客户端把 page/page_size 翻译为 skip/limit 字段发送。服务器不接受 skip/limit；若包含则会返回 422。  [FACT:request-skip-accepted] [FACT:request-limit-accepted] [FACT:request-invalid-status]
- 前端分页组件的页码从 1 开始（与 page 的定义一致）；当用户选择页码或 page_size 时，发起请求时使用 page 和 page_size，后端会基于内部偏移计算数据。  [FACT:pagination-offset]
- 对于 UX 行为：
  - 如果后端返回 data 为空数组且返回了真实 count，应显示“无数据”或禁用后续页码，但仍显示总条数（count）。  [FACT:response-empty-page-data] [FACT:response-count-scope]
  - 当收到 422（由于发送 skip/limit 或非法参数）时，向用户展示友好错误（例如“请求参数不被支持，请使用 page 和 page_size”），并记录日志以便排查。  [FACT:request-invalid-status]

前端实现细节建议：
- 在发起请求前统一做一层参数规范化函数：
  - 强制将 page/page_size 转为整数并套用缺省值（page default 1；page_size default 20）。
  - 校验 page >=1，page_size in [1,50]，非法时展示验证错误，不发送请求。
  - 严格禁止并移除任何 skip/limit 字段（若存在，阻止发送并在控制台/日志记录）。
- Pagination UI：总是以 1 作为第一页，向后端请求后根据返回的 count 渲染页数，若当前 page 超出末页，根据返回的 data=[] 与 count 渲染（禁用下一页）。

注意：后端负责把 page/page_size 转为内部 offset = (page-1)*page_size，用于查询（前端无需计算 offset）。  [FACT:pagination-offset]
packets.backend_prompt:
实现要点（后端）：

必须在后端接口解析/校验层严格遵循下列契约事实（逐项内嵌以便审计）：
[FACT:request-invalid-status]
[FACT:response-count-scope]
[FACT:response-empty-page-data]
[FACT:request-skip-accepted]
[FACT:request-limit-accepted]
[FACT:request-page-type]
[FACT:request-page-minimum]
[FACT:request-page-default]
[FACT:request-page-size-type]
[FACT:request-page-size-minimum]
[FACT:request-page-size-maximum]
[FACT:request-page-size-default]
[FACT:pagination-offset]

后端必须实现：
- 请求参数解析与校验：
  - 仅接受 page（integer）和 page_size（integer）。  [FACT:request-page-type] [FACT:request-page-size-type]
  - page 的最小值为 1，缺省为 1。  [FACT:request-page-minimum] [FACT:request-page-default]
  - page_size 的范围为 1—50，缺省为 20。  [FACT:request-page-size-minimum] [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default]
- 拒绝双协议：若请求包含 skip 或 limit 任何一个（query/body/header 等来源），必须返回 HTTP 422（request.invalid_status = 422）。不得接受 skip/limit。  [FACT:request-skip-accepted] [FACT:request-limit-accepted] [FACT:request-invalid-status]
- 内部偏移计算：根据 page 与 page_size 计算 offset = (page-1)*page_size，用于数据库查询（例如 LIMIT page_size OFFSET offset 或等价方式）。  [FACT:pagination-offset]
- 查询与响应约束：
  - 在应用权限过滤与排序后（但在分页前），计算并返回真实的 count（scope = authorized_filtered_before_pagination）。  [FACT:response-count-scope]
  - 然后基于 page_size/offset 获取 data 并返回。响应格式保持为 { data: [...], count: N }。
  - 若 page 超出最后一页，返回 data = [] 且 count 仍为真实总数（不要将 count 置为 0）。  [FACT:response-empty-page-data]

实现细节建议：
- 接口入口示例伪代码：
  - 从请求中提取参数；如果发现 skip 或 limit 则立即返回 422。
  - 将 page/page_size 转为整数；若缺失则填充默认值（page=1,page_size=20）。
  - 验证范围：page >=1；1 <= page_size <=50；验证失败返回 400（或按团队约定的参数错误码）。
  - 计算 offset = (page-1)*page_size，用于分页查询。
  - 先对数据做权限和过滤（以及排序），得到总 count（不受分页限制）。
  - 再带 LIMIT page_size OFFSET offset 获取 data。
  - 返回 { data, count }，并确保当 offset 超过可用数据时 data 为空数组而 count 为真实值。

日志与监控：
- 在拒绝包含 skip/limit 的请求时记录足够信息以便排查（请求来源、参数内容），并监控 422 的数量以发现客户端兼容性问题。

注意：不要引入新的分页协议或同时支持 skip/limit 与 page/page_size。必须保持单一协议为 page/page_size 并严格拒绝 skip/limit（见上述 FACT 标注）。

packets.frontend_prompt:
Implement UI and client-side behavior to match the authoritative contract facts and the rollback change. Key enforced constraints and behaviors (must match server):

- Title length ceiling and validation
  - Enforce max length = 80 code points on user-entered titles. Include this exact contract marker in the prompt text: [FACT:request-title-max-length]
  - Trim leading and trailing U+0020 (space) on user input before measuring length (request.title.trim = "U+0020").
  - Count length in Unicode code points (request.title.length_unit = "unicode_code_point").
  - Enforce minimum length = 3 code points on user-entered titles (request.title.min_length = 3). The minimum and trim rules are not to be revoked.
  - If the user explicitly submits a title that violates min/max after trim, show validation errors client-side and prevent submit; if the client nevertheless sends an invalid title, handle a 422 response gracefully.
  - Ensure the UI error for invalid title uses the expected server status: 422 (request.title.invalid_status = 422).

- Read and display behavior
  - Allow reading and displaying existing titles that are longer than 80 code points without truncation. This is required by contract: [FACT:read-existing-overlength-title-allowed]
  - Do not modify or silently truncate titles when rendering. If desirable, add a visual indicator (e.g., "overlength") but do not change stored value on read.

- Update semantics (partial updates)
  - Do not revalidate the existing stored title when the user omits the title field in an update request. This behavior is required: [FACT:update-omitted_title-revalidate]
  - Concretely: when submitting a partial update (PATCH) that omits title, do not block the update client-side due to the stored title's length; send the request without title and expect the server to accept it.
  - When the user explicitly edits/supplies title in an update, apply the same trim + length validation rules as on create.

- Create vs Update
  - Create flows must require a title (create.title.required = true); validate trim, length unit, min 3 and max 80 before submission.
  - Update flows must allow omitting title (update.title.required = false); omission means "unchanged" (update.title.omission = "unchanged").

- Description
  - Keep description max length = 500 (request.description.max_length = 500); validate on client-side similarly.
  - Do not change description trimming behavior: request.description.trim = false.

- Tests to include in frontend test-suite (automated + manual QA steps)
  1) Read test: fetch an existing asset whose stored title length is 100 code points. Confirm UI displays the full title unchanged. This validates [FACT:read-existing-overlength_title_allowed].
  2) Partial update test: start with an asset that has an existing 100-code-point title, open edit form, change only the description, leave title field empty/omitted, submit PATCH. Confirm client does NOT block the submission and server accepts the update (no title sent). This confirms partial update semantics ("已有 100 字 title，更新 description").
  3) Explicit overlength submit: attempt to edit title to 90+ code points, trim spaces, see client-side validation error; if bypassed, server responds 422 and UI surfaces the server validation error.
  4) Create test: try creating with title length <3 or >80 after trim; client must block and show error.

- Error handling and UX
  - Surface server 422 errors for title validation as field-level errors and preserve input for user correction.
  - If server returns an error due to title on update, ensure you treat it as an explicit-submission validation failure (different from omission behavior).

- Deployment notes
  - Do not attempt to migrate or rewrite stored titles on the client; preserve existing overlength titles when reading/updating.
  - Coordinate with backend to ensure version bump of the asset contract/schema is applied server-side when this change is deployed (backend will handle the version increment).
packets.backend_prompt:
Implement server-side validation and behavior to match the authoritative contract facts and rollback requirement. Required explicit contract markers must be observed in this prompt: [FACT:request-title-max-length] [FACT:read-existing-overlength-title-allowed] [FACT:update-omitted_title-revalidate]

Validation rules (apply on create and on requests that explicitly include title):
- Trim rule: Trim only U+0020 (space) from both ends of request.title before validation (request.title.trim = "U+0020").
- Length unit: measure title length in Unicode code points (request.title.length_unit = "unicode_code_point").
- Minimum: require at least 3 code points (request.title.min_length = 3). This lower bound must not be revoked.
- Maximum: reject titles longer than 80 code points (request.title.max_length = 80). When a submitted title violates max (or min), return HTTP 422 with a field-level error for title. Ensure the API uses the invalid status defined (request.title.invalid_status = 422).

Read and stored-data behavior:
- Allow existing stored titles that exceed 80 code points to be read and returned by the API (read.existing_overlength_title.allowed = true). Do not reject or rewrite existing data on reads.
- Do not perform automatic trimming/truncation of stored titles in read responses beyond the trim rule applied to incoming requests; do not silently alter stored values.

Update semantics (PATCH/PUT):
- If the request omits the title field entirely, do NOT revalidate the stored title. Omission means "unchanged"; accept the update regardless of the stored title's current length or validity. This is mandated: [FACT:update-omitted_title-revalidate]
  - Concretely, for PATCH: if 'title' is absent in the JSON payload, do not run title validators; leave stored title unchanged.
- If the request includes a title field (even if equal to the existing value), apply full validation: trim U+0020, count code points, enforce min and max; on violation return 422.

Create vs Update behavior:
- Create: title is required (create.title.required = true). Validate trim, min, max on create.
- Update: title is optional (update.title.required = false); omission = unchanged (update.title.omission = "unchanged").

Description behavior:
- Continue to enforce description.max_length = 500 (request.description.max_length = 500). request.description.trim = false (do not trim description by default).

Error responses and formats:
- Use HTTP 422 for validation failures on title and description. Provide a field-level error object identifying the field, the rule failed (e.g., "min_length", "max_length") and a human message.
- Example error payload for title too long:
  { "status": 422, "errors": [{ "field": "title", "code": "max_length", "message": "title must be at most 80 Unicode code points" }] }

Data migration and versioning:
- Do NOT rewrite or delete existing overlength titles as part of this change.
- Bump the asset/contract version or schema version as part of this deployment to indicate a rollback of the max length; ensure the new deployed version number is incremented (the asset version must continue to increase after this rollback).

Tests to include in backend test-suite (automated):
1) Read test: store a title of 100 Unicode code points; GET returns full stored title. Confirms [FACT:read-existing_overlength_title_allowed].
2) Partial update test: GIVEN stored title = 100 code points, accept PATCH that omits title but changes description; stored title remains unchanged and update succeeds. Confirms [FACT:update-omitted_title_revalidate].
3) Explicit update test: when client sends title trimmed to >80 code points, respond 422 with appropriate field-level error. Confirms [FACT:request-title-max-length].
4) Create test: reject title <3 or >80 after trimming with 422.

Implementation notes:
- Ensure trimming logic uses only U+0020; do not remove other whitespace by default.
- Use a Unicode-aware code point counter (not grapheme clusters unless contract changes) to measure length.
- Maintain backward compatibility for reads: existing overlength titles remain readable and unchanged until/if a future migration is explicitly specified.

Deployment coordination:
- Communicate to frontend that omitted-title updates will not revalidate stored title, and that overlength stored titles are expected and allowed to be read.
- Increment the asset/contract version upon deploying this change so consumers can observe that the contract was updated.

packets.raw_requirement: 前后端：page_size 默认值由 20 改为 25，上限由 50 改为 100。响应新增整数 page、page_size，回显实际生效值。
packets.frontend_prompt:
Implementation task for frontend team — make the client UI and request behavior follow the updated pagination contract. Must-read facts (include in implementation): [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default] [FACT:response-page-type] [FACT:response-page-value] [FACT:response-page-size-type] [FACT:response-page-size-value]

Requirements and actionable steps:
- Controls and defaults
  - Set the page_size control default to 25 and its maximum allowed input to 100. (Use [FACT:request-page-size-default] and [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] when setting UI defaults/limits.)
  - Ensure the page control defaults to 1 if the user does not supply a value.
  - Do not expose or allow skip/limit controls anywhere in the UI — these remain forbidden.

- Request composition
  - Send pagination using page and page_size (both integers). Do not send skip or limit.
  - If the user leaves page empty, omit it from the query so the server will apply the default (which is 1).

- Client-side validation and UX
  - Validate page_size client-side to accept integers >=1 and <=100. Allow 100 as a valid value; treat 101 (or any >100) as invalid and prevent the request. Show a clear validation message when page_size is out of range.
  - If the server returns validation errors (HTTP 422), display the server message and map it to the control state.

- Response handling and synchronization
  - Read the server-provided fields response.page and response.page_size, which are integers. (See [FACT:response-page-type], [FACT:response-page-value], [FACT:response-page-size-type], [FACT:response-page-size-value].)
  - After every request, override the UI controls to reflect the server-echoed effective values: set the page control to effective_page (response.page) and the page_size control to effective_page_size (response.page_size). This ensures the client always shows the actual page and page_size the backend applied.
  - Use the server-echoed values for any client-side pagination state or display (not the requested values), e.g. when enabling/disabling previous/next buttons.

- Internal client calculation
  - If you compute offsets locally for UI-only features, derive offset as (page-1)*page_size using the effective values returned by the server.

- Tests to add
  - Verify control default values: page_size default = 25 and max = 100.
  - Verify page omitted -> UI sends no page -> server defaults to page=1 and client reflects response.page = 1.
  - Verify page_size = 100 is accepted and the client displays the server-echoed page_size.
  - Verify page_size = 101 is rejected client-side; if sent, server responds 422 and the client surfaces the validation error.

Acceptance criteria
- UI controls show default page_size 25 and enforce max 100.
- After any request, the page and page_size controls reflect the integers returned by the server (effective_page, effective_page_size).
- No skip/limit inputs exist or are used in requests.

Include the required facts markers in any engineering notes, PR description, and automated tests: [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default] [FACT:response-page-type] [FACT:response-page-value] [FACT:response-page-size-type] [FACT:response-page-size-value].
packets.backend_prompt:
Implementation task for backend team — update request validation, defaults, and response to implement the new pagination contract. Must-read facts (include in implementation): [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default] [FACT:response-page-type] [FACT:response-page-value] [FACT:response-page-size-type] [FACT:response-page-size-value]

Requirements and actionable steps:
- Request validation and defaults
  - Enforce request.page as an integer with minimum 1 and default 1 when omitted.
  - Enforce request.page_size as an integer, minimum 1, default 25, maximum 100. (Apply [FACT:request-page-size-default] and [FACT:request-page-size-maximum].)
  - Reject any incoming skip or limit parameters; treat them as not accepted and respond with a validation error.

- Error handling
  - On invalid pagination parameters (e.g., non-integer, page < 1, page_size < 1 or page_size > 100, use of skip/limit), return HTTP 422 with a clear error payload describing the invalid field(s). (Use existing status behavior for invalid requests.)

- Response shape and echoing effective values
  - Add response fields page and page_size to the normal list response. Both fields must be integers. (See [FACT:response-page-type] and [FACT:response-page-size-type].)
  - Set response.page to the effective page used for the query and response.page_size to the effective page_size used; use the exact semantic names effective_page and effective_page_size in code/comments as the values being echoed. (See [FACT:response-page-value] and [FACT:response-page-size-value].)
  - The client relies on these echoed values to update its UI; ensure they always reflect any server-side adjustments.

- Pagination internals
  - Compute the data fetch offset using offset = (page - 1) * page_size. Use the effective page and page_size values when computing offset.

- Behavioral requirements and edge cases
  - Accept page_size = 100 as valid and process normally.
  - Reject page_size = 101 (and any >100) with HTTP 422.
  - If page is omitted, treat as page = 1.
  - Ensure existing semantics for count and empty-page responses remain unchanged; e.g., count scope and empty data list behavior should not be altered by this change.

- Tests to add
  - Unit tests for request validation: missing page -> default 1; page_size default 25; page_size boundary tests (1, 100 valid; 101 invalid).
  - Integration tests verifying the full response includes page and page_size integers with the effective values and that pagination offset is applied to data selection.
  - Tests verifying skip and limit parameters are rejected.

- Deployment notes
  - Bump any API documentation and client-facing docs to show page_size default 25 and max 100, and document that the response will echo page and page_size (integers).

Include the required facts markers in PR descriptions, API spec updates, and tests: [FACT:request-page-size-maximum] [FACT:request-page-size-default] [FACT:response-page-type] [FACT:response-page-value] [FACT:response-page-size-type] [FACT:response-page-size-value].

Implement the client-side behavior for item create (POST /api/v1/items/) and item update (PUT /api/v1/items/{id}) to exactly match the contract rules below:

1) Pre-submit processing and validation
- Before any validation or submitting to the server, trim only U+0020 (ASCII space) from both ends of the entered title value. Do not normalize or trim other Unicode whitespace.
- Measure title length in Unicode code points (not bytes, not UTF-16 code units) after trimming.
- Enforce minimum length = 3 and maximum length = 80. Values with length < 3 or > 80 must be rejected client-side where possible.
- Titles that become empty or all-space after trimming must be treated as invalid.
